title: Seizure + anticholinergic toxidrome + QRS widening after psych discharge: tricyclic antidepressant overdose
vignette: A 17-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department by a friend an hour after she was observed having a seizure. The patient has no known history of a seizure disorder. Her friend reports she has a history of depression and substance use disorder and was released yesterday from a psychiatric hospital after 3 days of inpatient treatment. The patient's medications are unknown. Temperature is 38.3 C (100.9 F), blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg, and pulse is 130/min. On examination, the patient is sedated and disoriented. The pupils are dilated and bowel sounds are decreased. She has 700 mL of urine return when a urinary catheter is placed. ECG reveals sinus tachycardia and a QRS duration of 130 msec. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

clues.note: Depression is a common indication for tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), which are dangerous in overdose and available to psychiatric patients.

clues.text: pupils are dilated and bowel sounds are decreased
clues.note: Mydriasis with decreased bowel sounds (plus hyperthermia, flushing, tachycardia) is an ANTICHOLINERGIC toxidrome - a hallmark of TCA overdose.

clues.text: 700 mL of urine return when a urinary catheter is placed
clues.note: Urinary retention (large bladder volume on catheterization) is another anticholinergic effect.
QRS WIDENING (130 / normal <120 msec) from cardiac fast sodium-channel blockade is the dangerous cardiotoxic signature of TCA overdose (arrhythmia risk).

whatMatters: New-onset seizure + ANTICHOLINERGIC toxidrome (dilated pupils, decreased bowel sounds, urinary retention, hyperthermia, tachycardia) + QRS WIDENING and hypotension = TRICYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANT OVERDOSE (multi-receptor blockade). Answer F.
strategy: Assemble the TCA overdose triad: (1) CNS (seizures, sedation - GABA-A/muscarinic and histamine block); (2) ANTICHOLINERGIC signs (mydriasis, ileus, retention, hyperthermia); (3) CARDIAC toxicity (QRS widening from fast-Na-channel block, hypotension from alpha-1 block). Reject cocaine overdose (would be HYPERtension + diaphoresis, not hypotension/dry-anticholinergic/QRS widening), benzodiazepine/opioid withdrawal, salicylate toxicity (tinnitus, mixed acid-base, no QRS widening/anticholinergic), and serotonin syndrome (hyperreflexia/clonus, diaphoresis, hypertension - no QRS widening).

eliminations.label: Benzodiazepine withdrawal - no anticholinergic/QRS
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: withdrawal causing seizures, tremor, tachycardia, agitation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't cause anticholinergic signs (dry, dilated, retention) or QRS widening/hypotension. ✅ Correct if: seizures with autonomic hyperactivity after stopping a benzodiazepine (no QRS widening).

eliminations.label: Cocaine overdose - hypertension/diaphoresis expected
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sympathomimetic toxicity (seizures, hyperthermia, tachycardia, MI). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: cocaine causes HYPERtension and DIAPHORESIS (wet skin), not the hypotension and dry anticholinergic picture/QRS widening seen here. ✅ Correct if: hypertensive, diaphoretic, agitated with chest pain.

eliminations.label: Opioid withdrawal - hypertension, diarrhea
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: withdrawal with dilated pupils, mild fever, hypertension, diarrhea/cramps. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't cause seizures, cardiac conduction delay, decreased bowel sounds, or hypotension. ✅ Correct if: mydriasis with GI hyperactivity and hypertension after stopping opioids.

eliminations.label: Salicylate toxicity - tinnitus, mixed acid-base
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: aspirin toxicity (hyperthermia, altered mental status, seizures from neuroglycopenia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it presents with tinnitus, tachypnea, and a mixed respiratory alkalosis/anion-gap metabolic acidosis - not QRS widening, urinary retention, or dilated pupils. ✅ Correct if: tinnitus + mixed acid-base disturbance.

eliminations.label: Serotonin syndrome - clonus/hyperreflexia, hypertension
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: excess serotonergic activity (agitation, hyperthermia, neuromuscular hyperactivity). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it features hyperreflexia/CLONUS, diaphoresis, and hypertension - not QRS widening or the dry anticholinergic picture. ✅ Correct if: clonus/hyperreflexia after serotonergic drugs.

reasoning: New-onset seizure with sedation, hyperthermia, and tachycardia after psychiatric discharge
Anticholinergic signs: dilated pupils, decreased bowel sounds, urinary retention
ECG shows QRS widening (fast sodium-channel block) with hypotension (alpha-1 block)
mechanism: TRICYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANTS (TCAs; e.g., amitriptyline, nortriptyline) block MULTIPLE receptors/channels, so overdose produces a characteristic multi-system picture: (1) CNS effects - SEIZURES (GABA-A antagonism), SEDATION/coma (H1 antihistamine), and agitation/delirium (central muscarinic block); (2) ANTICHOLINERGIC toxicity from muscarinic blockade - hyperthermia, dry/flushed skin, MYDRIASIS (dilated pupils), tachycardia, DECREASED bowel sounds (ileus), and URINARY RETENTION; and (3) CARDIOVASCULAR toxicity - blockade of cardiac FAST SODIUM CHANNELS slows phase 0 depolarization, causing QRS WIDENING (>100-120 msec) with risk of ventricular arrhythmia, and alpha-1 blockade causes HYPOTENSION. Cardiac toxicity is the major cause of death; treatment of QRS widening/arrhythmia is IV SODIUM BICARBONATE (increases extracellular sodium and alkalinizes, relieving Na-channel block). This patient - recently discharged from psychiatric care (TCA access), with a seizure, anticholinergic signs, hypotension, and QRS widening - fits TCA overdose. The distractors (cocaine, salicylate, serotonin syndrome, benzodiazepine/opioid withdrawal) each lack the QRS widening plus anticholinergic-with-hypotension combination.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Pharm > TCA overdose: block muscarinic (anticholinergic), H1 (sedation), alpha-1 (hypotension), GABA-A (seizures), and cardiac fast Na channels (QRS widening, arrhythmia); treat QRS widening with sodium bicarbonate; cardiotoxicity is the main cause of death.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Seizure + anticholinergic signs + QRS widening + hypotension = TCA overdose.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on anticholinergic toxidrome, QRS widening, fast sodium-channel block, alpha-1 blockade, or sodium bicarbonate treatment? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Cocaine = hypertension/diaphoresis; salicylate = tinnitus/mixed acid-base; serotonin syndrome = clonus/hypertension; withdrawals lack QRS widening.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: TCA overdose = anticholinergic + seizures + QRS widening/hypotension; treat with sodium bicarbonate.
